title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
summary: Mark every prime up to n once, then answer primality queries in O(1) each.
usage: Start crossing out at `i*i` (smaller multiples were already removed by smaller primes) and stop the outer loop at `sqrt(n)`. Use a compact array (`bitset`, `vector<bool>` or a byte array) so n up to about 10^7 fits in memory. Use `long long` for `i*i` in C++/Java when n is near 2^31. To factorise quickly, store the smallest prime factor per number instead of a boolean.
